descriptionText: GitHub Actions workflows that check for bot actors using spoofable contexts like github.actor or github.triggering_actor can be bypassed by attackers. These contexts can be manipulated by creating usernames that end with '[bot]' or match bot IDs. For example, an attacker could create a user named 'malicious-dependabot[bot]' to bypass security checks. Workflows triggered by events like pull_request_target, issues, issue_comment, and others should use event-specific user contexts (e.g., github.event.pull_request.user.login, github.event.comment.user.login) instead. The rule identifies bot checks in both dominating conditions (like 'github.actor == dependabot[bot]' or checks with OR operators) which always pass for matching actors, and non-dominating conditions (with AND operators) which depend on other factors. Known vulnerable bot IDs include: 29110 (dependabot integration ID), 49699333 (dependabot[bot]), 27856297 (dependabot-preview[bot]), and 29139614 (renovate[bot]).
